title: Yehudah bar Natan

paragraphs: In [Berakhot 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.60a.18) he walks behind Rav Hamnuna and sighs. Rav Hamnuna asks, “Do you want to bring suffering upon yourself? It is written, ‘What I feared…’” Yehudah asks, “But isn’t it written, ‘Happy is the person who always fears’?” Rav Hamnuna replies that the verse refers to matters of Torah. Hyman cites the Dikdukei Soferim reading: R' Yehudah, son of R' Natan, was walking in Rabbi’s locale, in the market of Tiberias, etc.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: In the linked Bavli, Yehudah walks behind Rav Hamnuna. Yehudah sighs and Rav Hamnuna responds.
[Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1703&lang=en) also places Yehudah with Rav Hamnuna.

The manuscript column in [Dikdukei Soferim, Berakhot, p. 342](https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/ZWuq1txyjt8C?hl=en&gbpv=1&pg=PA342) places him in Rabbi’s locale, in the market of Tiberias. The print column has him following Rav Hamnuna. The manuscript wording does not name Rabbi.
